chunks: And from him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"My father left behind sixty slaves, and he bequeathed their manumission for one-third of them. So I cast lots among them, and twenty were selected, and I freed them."
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams handle the manumission of slaves when only a portion was bequeathed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of *wasiyya* (bequest) regarding slaves, where Imam al-Baqir (AS) fulfilled his father's instruction to free one-third of his sixty slaves. The use of casting lots (*qur'a*) to select the specific individuals highlights a recognized juristic method for ensuring fairness and impartiality when the beneficiaries are not individually specified. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on the emancipation of slaves as a form of voluntary charity and debt fulfillment within the framework of inheritance law.
